statement: Every contribution and synthesis packet cited by an assertion remains present and unchanged
description: Replacement with different content and omission during whole-scope import are refused through the store's shared cited-evidence predicates.

statement: Build a real-time collaborative Convex backend with full CRUD, graph queries, and traceability functions
description: Convex backend at provenance/convex/ with 10 tables, 27 indexes, entity modules for all artifact types, graph.ts with 9 query functions (getCanvasScope, getDepthScope, getRootOverview, traceForward, traceBackward, findGaps, findStale, findOrphans, getCoverageStats), HTTP API endpoints, and WorkOS JWT authentication.

statement: Build a static analysis scanner in the Statesman CLI that extracts rule annotations from source code and reports coverage to Provenance, giving external tests access to the full traceability, impact analysis, gap detection, and audit trail capabilities
description: The scanner traverses a codebase, finds test files, extracts @statesman annotations (mirroring contract metadata: name, description, tags, rule, coverage, confidence), and pushes structured coverage to the broker via RuleContract with mapping_source=imported. By living in the CLI, external tests become first-class citizens in the Provenance graph: traceability queries show them alongside contracts, traceForward surfaces affected tests when sources change, findGaps detects rules with no coverage from any source, the UI renders them in the same canvas, all writes carry audit trails, and CI pipelines get coverage reporting with one additional step. Output JSON for machine consumption. Handle comment syntax variations across languages. Includes scan-time validation: cross-reference extracted annotations against active project rules and warn on unknown rule codes, deprecated rules, archived rules to prevent false coverage confidence. Every invocation scans all matching files; incremental scanning by content hash or git change detection is a deliberate non-goal for the first version (absorbed from deleted rule PROV-SCAN-012).

statement: Each parent artifact has one deterministic canonical active thread after a posting write
description: The oldest active thread wins with lower id breaking timestamp ties, and the posting write archives every other active sibling.

statement: Every CLI flag family that constructs a record is complete before that record is parsed or written
description: Required fields have equal cardinality; optional fields are absent or have the same cardinality.

statement: A confidence outside the finite unit interval is never silently clamped
description: Graph records reject invalid scores; source annotations warn at the line and retain the default while sharing core's validity verdict.

description: The system shall support the complete research lifecycle: capturing sources, decomposing requirements, recording design resolutions, and deriving enforceable rules — all linked in a traceable knowledge graph so that any rule can be explained back to its originating requirement and source material.

statement: The default wiki output is added to .gitignore without rewriting existing entries
description: The generated default path is appended only when absent and remains idempotent across repeated builds and line-ending styles; explicit output paths leave .gitignore untouched.

statement: Define an annotation format that mirrors Statesman's existing contract metadata vocabulary for declaring rule coverage in external test code
description: Adopt Allure's label/link primitive model but use Statesman's own vocabulary. The annotation fields replicate what contracts already carry: name, description, tags (from Contract trait), rule code, coverage level, confidence, notes (from RuleContract join). Per-language native APIs (Python decorators, Rust attributes, Java annotations, JS/TS functions) all serialize to the same output format. Comment-based annotations as the zero-dependency universal baseline. Explicitly NO epic/feature/story -- Statesman is not a project management tool. The requirement tree provides hierarchy; Provenance derives structural context from the rule's graph chain. The comment form is the zero-dependency baseline that works in any language; per-language native APIs (decorators, attributes) would be optional sugar serialising to the same output (absorbed from deleted rule PROV-ANNOT-003).

statement: Detect and report stale annotations where rule codes reference rules that no longer exist or have been deprecated
description: As rules evolve (deprecated, archived, superseded), annotations in test code can go stale. The scanner should cross-reference extracted annotations against the project's active rules and flag mismatches: unknown rule codes, deprecated rules, archived rules. This prevents false coverage confidence.

statement: An edge that violates endpoint constraints is rejected at write time, never stored and repaired later
Expose parent-id filtering on 'statesman provenance requirements list' to allow listing children of a specific requirement without client-side filtering
description: The Convex backend has getChildren but the CLI only exposes list with project-id scoping. Agents and humans working with requirement trees need to list children directly. Add --parent-id flag to requirements list that delegates to the getChildren query.

statement: The shaping frontier is computed from graph semantics by one shared function that prime, the gaps command, and the wiki assembler all call; no surface keeps its own gap taxonomy
description: docs/shaping.md stakes the design on a computed frontier, but the code had drifted three ways: find_gaps computed one gap kind, the wiki independently computed seven, and the shaping skill assembled the frontier by hand from five list commands - the hand-wiring the design forbids. The eleven gap kinds are the reconciled union plus the three shaping.md named that nobody computed.

statement: Every graph id is non-empty and uses only lowercase ASCII letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen
description: Private id newtypes route construction and deserialization through one predicate, with emitted schema patterns checked against the same verdict.

statement: A graph reference is an exact, reverified identity for one committed graph
description: Issuance stores a full commit and typed hash fields; every read rederives repository identity, graph digest, and reference id before returning the graph.

statement: An automated ideation run must be budgeted and cancellable before it starts, idempotent when a step is retried, inspectable after it ends, and unable to change a canonical record until a human promotes the proposal.
description: Compressed from the 27 run-machinery rules among the 38 imported PROV-IDEATE records (the other eleven: six were tests written as rules, five superseded by bound rules by shipped rules) written for the Statesman cloud ideation runner and never built. Their themes, kept so nothing is lost silently: a run targets one artifact and posts participant comments plus a synthesis to that artifact's thread; a stable run id ties the work item, participant executions, comments, synthesis, proposal cards, retries and promotions together; an explicit status lifecycle (queued, running, synthesizing, succeeded, partial, failed_retryable, failed_terminal, cancelled) never reports a run with a failed participant as succeeded; an input snapshot records target, sources, graph scope, profile and prompt versions, models and budgets; maximums for participants, rounds, model calls, tokens, wall-clock and generated bytes are enforced before execution and fail the run visibly; cancellation and deadlines stop new work, keep finished output and mark unfinished slots; participant writes are keyed deterministically so a retried slot updates one logical output instead of duplicating it; failures carry the failed step, retry state and diagnostics, and unsafe output is recorded as a sanitized marker rather than posted; participant comments carry stance, strongest finding, evidence references, risks, objections, suggested changes, uncertainty and open questions, and a challenge names the comment it challenges; synthesis preserves consensus, contested claims, minority objections, evidence gaps and open questions instead of collapsing them, stays short enough to read as a brief, and emits typed proposal cards recording their origin comments, claims, evidence level, dissent, confidence and target, with duplicates merged or marked; a promoted artifact links back to the run, synthesis, origin comments, proposal card and approval event; the thread shows outcomes before transcripts, keeps raw output as secondary, and shows the persona label apart from the executing identity; a run reads and writes only inside its target's scope and respects source access and redaction. What shipped instead is the proposal, assertion and disposition model in the ideation records; none of the run machinery above exists.

source_refs.clause: Productionising persona ideation: run lifecycle, budgets, idempotent writes, dissent-preserving synthesis, human promotion

statement: Implement a normalized knowledge graph data model with 4 core artifact types (Source, Requirement, Resolution, Rule) and typed graph edges
description: The data model uses separate tables per artifact type with a junction table for 9 typed graph edges (references, refines_into, depends_on, contradicts, supersedes, needs, resolves, spawns, produces). Requirements recurse to arbitrary depth via parentId. Each artifact carries its own status lifecycle.

statement: A pinned graph contains only canonical records owned by its selected scope
description: Collaboration and ideation families and fields are excluded, and every projected record must name the scope whose digest and counts the reference records.

statement: Undisposed proposals enter work only through an exact cited path or explicit typed territory
description: Proposals remain evidence-backed context outside Prime and global review; current work surfaces only records whose recorded evidence or target exactly matches its territory.

statement: A proposal's accepted, rejected, or deferred state is read only from an immutable disposition record naming an allowlisted actor; no writer sets a proposal row past proposed, and every read derives effective state rather than trusting the row
description: The legacy backtrace landed 153 proposals and batch disposal never happened, so unrefuted swarm-asserted proposals became a legitimate resting state. A writable promotion_state column is forgeable and non-atomic against the decision history it must agree with. Actor ids are audit attestations under repository access, not cryptographic identity proof.

statement: Provenance shall support structured multi-persona ideation threads for artifact review and requirement discovery
description: The system shall let automated jobs convene 3-5 distinct persona-style agents around a target requirement, source, resolution, rule, or problem. The agents leave attributable thread comments, challenge one another, and produce a synthesis that helps humans discover requirements, risks, rules, resolutions, and open questions while preserving dissent and traceability.

source_refs.clause: User-validated pattern: named agents ideating in Provenance threads produce useful design outcomes and should be productionised as bounded automated review jobs

statement: Provide a durable thread and message discussion system attachable to any artifact
description: Threads attach to any artifact type (requirement, source, resolution, rule, topic, question) with status lifecycle (active, resolved, archived). Messages carry role (user, assistant, system) for attributing human vs AI-authored content. Convenience CLI command auto-creates threads.

statement: A record claiming an unsupported schema version is refused before conversion or rewrite
description: Readers check raw stored versions before deserialization, and read-modify-write paths leave a shard byte-identical when any row claims a future layout.

statement: Every resolution input has a nonblank reference and summary
description: The fields name what informed the decision without requiring an external law, file, or conversation to be a graph record.

statement: A resolved requirement without a decision or rule is labelled with that absence
description: Plain Resolved is reserved for requirements backed by at least one decision or rule; all other statuses retain their ordinary label.

statement: A Provenance rule is a function in the codebase, or a type whose construction is the proof; the graph record is its handle, bound by a compiled marker
description: There is no rule engine, no primitive, and no runtime: the marker moves with refactors, dies with deleted code, and the scanner reads the binding from source. Rules follow human decisions, not code structure - one function with many branches can be one rule, and a decision with no function yet is a requirement whose rule is unwritten.

statement: Every rule is produced by a requirement or a resolution, and rules are leaf nodes: no edge type may end below a rule
A shaping claim exists only while the record's status admits agent work
description: Closed topics and answered or human-blocked questions reject new claims, and transition into any such status clears an existing claim.

statement: Requirements and resolutions are wired through typed edges: a requirement needs a resolution; a resolution resolves its requirement and can spawn new requirements
The skills installer deletes a file left by an earlier install only when the content hash embedded in that file's own header matches the bytes on disk
description: The rename to provenance-prefixed skills orphaned four legacy skill directories and an AGENTS.md marker block in a flat shared namespace users may have authored into, so deletion by path alone risks user files. One changed byte fails the check and the file survives; the binary version string in the header is excluded from the hash so a version bump alone never orphans a file.

statement: A skill install never destroys a target it did not create unless force is passed
description: Missing targets may be written and identical managed output is retained; foreign files, directories, and symlinks are not replaced without explicit force.

statement: A skill-install run reports the strongest per-file effect in the order updated, installed, unchanged
description: Rewritten or removed files make the run updated; only additions make it installed; an empty or matching run is unchanged.

statement: A source commit pin contains 7 through 64 ASCII hexadecimal characters
description: Mixed case and abbreviated locators are accepted for evidence sources; graph-reference identities keep their stricter full lowercase commit shape.

statement: Every requirement is traceable to a motivating source via a references edge; requirements without one are surfaced as gaps, not rejected

Two branches editing different records in the same state shard merge with no human intervention: the merge driver keys on each record's stable id, takes the side that moved when only one moved, and reports a typed conflict naming the record when both moved differently
description: Canonical state is sharded JSONL in git specifically so git carries history; a record is one line, so git's own line merge collides textually on trivially reconcilable edits. The shipped .gitattributes.example wires state shards to the provenance merge-jsonl driver. The finer arms (ours-wins on divergence, delete-modify keeps the survivor and reports) are recorded from the code; no discussion of alternatives at that resolution exists.

statement: Support external test coverage linking via source-code annotations and static analysis, enabling rule traceability without requiring adoption of the Statesman contract framework
description: Not all tests fit into Statesman's contract scope (perf tests, unit tests, existing suites). Teams need a low-friction way to annotate existing tests in any language to declare which Provenance rules they enforce. A static analysis scanner extracts these annotations and reports coverage to Provenance, creating traceability links from rules to external test evidence.

statement: Support forward and backward traceability queries across the full artifact chain
description: Forward traceability: Source -> Requirements -> Resolutions -> Rules (what's affected when a source changes). Backward traceability: Rule -> Resolution -> Requirement -> Source (why does this rule exist). Both exposed via CLI commands and HTTP API endpoints.

source_refs.clause: Traceability: forward (source changed, what's affected) and backward (why does this rule exist)

statement: The broker must enforce multi-tenant security across all API endpoints
description: Covers authentication pipeline (Bearer-only, JWT RS256, API key delegation), authorization model (hierarchical permissions, RequirePermission extractors), tenant isolation (project-scoped SQL, ownership verification, cross-org prevention), input validation (progressive validation, pagination caps, config validation), information leakage prevention (404-not-403, token prefix logging, generic errors), infrastructure security (timeouts, fail-closed, parameterized SQL), and audit trail (project_id tracing, identity attribution, content-addressed dedup) for all broker HTTP handlers, services, and storage repositories.

statement: The Provenance CLI list commands shall support filtering by field values and configurable sort order
description: Currently list commands return all artifacts sorted newest-first with no filtering. At scale (73+ rules), this makes targeted queries impossible without client-side processing. Need: --filter 'severity=critical', --filter 'ruleCode=NS-01*', --sort=oldest, --sort=rule-code. Applies to rules list, requirements list, resolutions list, sources list.

statement: The Provenance CLI shall support bulk import and export of artifacts in JSON or TOML format
description: Creating 59 rules required 59 separate CLI calls. A bulk operation (statesman provenance rules import rules.json) would reduce this to one call. Export enables backup, migration, and offline review. Format should match the JSON output of list commands for round-trip compatibility.

statement: The Provenance CLI shall support direct lookup of artifacts by their domain identifier (rule_code for rules, slug for sources, etc.) without requiring pagination through list results
description: Currently the only way to find a rule by its code (e.g. NS-015) is to paginate through the full list sorted newest-first. With 73 rules at 50 per page, this is unusable for both humans and agents. Need: statesman provenance rules get --rule-code NS-015. Same pattern for other artifact types with domain identifiers.

statement: The Provenance thread post command shall reliably create threads and post messages on any artifact type without intermittent failures
description: During noscope planning, 3 of 6 agent sessions failed to post thread comments on rules. Errors included 'artifact not found' for valid artifact IDs. Earlier agents in the same session succeeded with identical commands. Root cause unclear: possibly auth token expiry mid-session, Convex HTTP endpoint routing, or rate limiting. Thread posting is critical for agent-driven review workflows.

statement: A proposal is asserted only by an owning synthesis whose positive support is uncontested and unblocked
description: The synthesis adjudicates exactly that proposal, has no blocking gap or pending human decision, and cites no unsupported or exploratory claim as positive evidence.

statement: Wiki domain membership follows requirement refinement ancestry and carries through to derived rules
description: Requirements retain their own domain and inherit ancestor domains; rules inherit the effective domains of their producing requirements.

statement: The wiki homepage must give one reader entry mode control of the first viewport at corpus scale.
description: The entry mode must be chosen among query-first retrieval, authored-domain orientation, and assurance-first corpus health. Evidence: PR #45 research, Fork assessment and Directions A-C.

source_refs.clause: Fork assessment; Directions A-C; candidate measurable constraints

statement: A wiki page distinguishes same-titled record links with stable record identity
description: Same-titled links receive the shortest distinct id suffix, with a minimum of eight characters; the record kind appears only when kind is the remaining distinction.

statement: The wiki generator destroys an output directory only on proof it owns it: a recognized ownership marker naming this generator at a supported version, an empty directory, or the generator-owned default output
description: Publication replaces the whole directory, so a wrong ownership answer deletes the caller's files. Foreign generator, unknown version, oversized, malformed, not-a-regular-file, and non-empty unmarked directories are refused with a typed error naming the path, leaving it untouched. Ownership is never inferred from a transaction-shaped filename, parseable journal, or nonce, and ambiguous crash residue is reported for operator choice, never auto-deleted.

statement: Wiki references stay plain text unless Provenance can form a working web or hosted-code URL
description: Existing web addresses pass through; known code hosts produce blob URLs; unknown remotes, prose, and ambiguous dotted tokens remain text.
